newsitem.title: CAMEROON: China to mine Cameroon's bauxite.
newsitem.headline: China to mine Cameroon's bauxite.

text.p: China is to mine Cameroonian bauxite under a weekend deal signed by visiting Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng, a senior official of Cameroon's mining ministry said.

Chinese company Gansu Corporation for International Techno-Economic Cooperation, GITEC, will mine the mineral following the conclusion of negotiations begun in 1992, the official told Reuters on Sunday.
No predictions were given for the amount of bauxite which the Chinese would mine, or when production would start.

The bauxite, an estimated two billion tonnes at three sites, would enable Cameroon to supply its Edea smelter, which currently uses alumina imported from Guinea. The Edea smelter is run by ALUCAM, a subsidiary of French group Pechiney and produces 80,000 tonnes of aluminum metal per year.
Cameroon's President Paul Biya, at an official dinner for the Chinese delegation, said he hoped China would eventually begin processing raw materials in Cameroon.
The Central African state's export economy is currently based on crude oil and agricultural products. --Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
